about.title: San Luis Obispo Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Luis Obispo is a small, walkable city, but that doesn't mean people here are immune from defective products — a faulty vehicle part on US-101 Southbound, a malfunctioning appliance in a Higuera Street apartment, or a poorly designed tool used on a Cal Poly job site can all cause serious harm. Under California law, injured people generally don't have to prove a manufacturer was negligent; strict liability often applies if the product itself was defective in design, manufacturing, or warnings, and that defect caused the injury. Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially share responsibility. If you were hurt by a product anywhere in San Luis Obispo County, keeping the item itself — rather than discarding or repairing it — can matter a great deal to a future claim. We evaluate what happened and explain your options directly.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California often allows product liability claims to proceed under strict liability, meaning the focus is generally on whether the product was defective and caused harm, not on proving carelessness. We can review the specifics of your situation and explain how this applies.

items.question: I was hurt by a product near Los Osos Valley Road — does location matter?
items.answer: Where the injury happened in San Luis Obispo County is less important than preserving evidence of the product itself and documenting how the injury occurred. We can help sort out these details regardless of the specific street or intersection involved.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in at the time of the injury, without repairing, altering, or discarding it. The product itself is often key evidence in a defect claim, so storing it safely can matter.
